passage: A public bench may appear to be a minor piece of street furniture, yet its position can shape who is able to use a neighbourhood. Older residents and people with limited mobility often plan journeys around reliable places to rest. Benches near shade, crossings and public toilets therefore extend the practical distance that some residents can travel independently. Designers sometimes remove seating to discourage long stays, but that response can also exclude people who need short, legitimate pauses. A more balanced approach considers visibility, maintenance and several seating heights rather than treating every user as a problem.
